pois: Washington Park
Washington Park is a city owned waterfront park on Fidalgo Island with a paved loop drive, beaches, and a boat launch.
Causland Memorial Park
Causland Memorial Park sits in downtown Anacortes and is known for its decorative rock masonry and landscaped gardens honoring veterans.
Anacortes Community Forest Lands

Anacortes History Museum
The Anacortes History Museum is housed in the historic former city hall and documents the town's maritime and industrial past.
Deception Pass State Park
Deception Pass State Park lies at the south end of Fidalgo Island and is one of the most visited parks in the Washington State Parks system.
Arlington City Hall
Arlington City Hall stands near Third Street and Olympic Avenue in the heart of downtown Arlington.
Haller Park
Haller Park sits along the Stillaguamish River and is one of the most facility rich parks in the city.
Legion Memorial Park
Legion Memorial Park is a gathering spot in downtown Arlington and connects to the regional trail system.
Centennial Trail
The Centennial Trail is a paved rail trail that runs through downtown Arlington and links communities across Snohomish County.
Whitehorse Trail
The Whitehorse Trail is a Snohomish County rail trail planned to connect Arlington toward Darrington.
Veterans Memorial Park
Veterans Memorial Park is a community park near downtown Auburn adjacent to the high school stadium.
Isaac Evans Park
Isaac Evans Park is a riverfront park along the Green River offering trails and passive recreation.
Game Farm Park
Game Farm Park is a large Auburn park with sports fields, picnic areas, and playgrounds.
Les Gove Park
Les Gove Park is a central community park that hosts gatherings and nearby city facilities.
Auburn Pioneer Cemetery
Auburn Pioneer Cemetery dates to the 1860s and is recognized as a city and county landmark.
Fay Bainbridge Park

Battle Point Park
Battle Point Park is a large community park with walking paths, playfields, and ponds near the center of the island.
Bloedel Reserve
Bloedel Reserve is a public garden and forest preserve with themed gardens and woodland walking trails.

Winslow Way

Bellevue Downtown Park
Bellevue Downtown Park is a central city park featuring a wide circular waterfall, open green, and playground framed by the skyline.
Bellevue Botanical Garden
The Bellevue Botanical Garden spans dozens of acres of cultivated gardens, woodlands, and wetlands open to the public.
Bellevue City Hall
Bellevue City Hall is the civic center for city government in downtown Bellevue.
Bellevue Arts Museum
The Bellevue Arts Museum is a downtown cultural venue focused on art, craft, and design.
Mercer Slough Nature Park
Mercer Slough area wetlands offer boardwalk trails and an environmental education center near downtown Bellevue.
Black Diamond Historical Museum
The Black Diamond Historical Museum occupies the town's former railroad depot and preserves its coal mining heritage.
Lake Sawyer Regional Park
Lake Sawyer Regional Park spans more than one hundred acres along one of the largest natural lakes in King County.
Black Diamond Open Space
The Black Diamond Open Space adds over a thousand acres of forested land and trails near the city.
Black Diamond Cemetery
The Black Diamond Cemetery is a recognized historical landmark tied to the town's early mining families.
KJ Gardner Skatepark
The KJ Gardner Skatepark is a large concrete skate facility built by the city for residents.
Allan Yorke Park

Lake Ken Simmons Park
Lake Ken Simmons Park offers a playground, a non motorized boat launch, and a swim area.
Fennel Creek Trail
The Fennel Creek Trail is a city trail that follows the creek corridor through Bonney Lake.
Lake Tapps

Bonney Lake Historical Society Museum
The Bonney Lake Historical Society operates a small museum in a former city hall building near Allan Yorke Park.
Park at Bothell Landing

Blyth Park
Blyth Park offers trails, playground equipment, and disc golf connecting to the Sammamish River Trail.
North Creek Forest
North Creek Forest is a wooded nature preserve protecting mature trees and habitat within the city.
Bothell City Hall
Bothell City Hall is the central hub for city government services downtown.
Sammamish River Trail
The Sammamish River Trail is a paved regional trail running through Bothell toward Seattle and Redmond.
Reuben A. Knoblauch Heritage Park
This downtown gathering place features a gazebo and a waterfall wall honoring local history.
Ryan House Museum
This historic home once belonged to the city's first elected mayor and now showcases local artifacts.
Sumner Link Trail
This paved multi use path follows the White River and connects to city parks for walking, running, and cycling.

This landmark furniture store doubles as a local visitor stop with model trains running overhead.
Sumner Cemetery

Museum of Glass

This pedestrian bridge connects the Museum of Glass to downtown and is lined with Dale Chihuly glass installations.
Washington State History Museum
This downtown museum presents exhibits on the history of Washington state and the Pacific Northwest.
Stadium High School
This landmark school occupies a French chateau style building originally planned as a hotel in the 1890s.
Tenino City Park
This central park offers picnic areas, a playground, ball fields, and a quarry pool for swimming.

This museum houses local artifacts including the original press used to make Depression era wooden money.

This civic building is made from the distinctive local sandstone that the town is known for quarrying.
Monarch Sculpture Park
This nonprofit contemporary sculpture park serves as a center for the arts on about five acres.
Fort Dent Park
This large park offers soccer fields, a playground, and a disc golf course near the Green River.

Duwamish Hill Preserve
This natural area offers trails and views across the surrounding Green River valley.

Tukwila Community Center
This community center provides a fitness center, gym courts, and programs for residents of all ages.

Pioneer Park
This community park offers sports fields and scenic river views on land owned by the City of Tumwater.

Tumwater Historical Park
This riverside park provides picnic facilities and access to the Deschutes River.

Curran Apple Orchard Park
This community orchard features more than 200 apple trees, picnic areas, and walking trails.
Cirque Park
This neighborhood park provides athletic fields, a skate park, playgrounds, and picnic areas.

Wilmot Gateway Park
This popular park includes a children's play area and sits near the Sammamish River Trail.
Columbia Winery

Woodinville Heritage Society Museum
This museum is housed in the preserved 1931 DeYoung House and presents local history exhibits.

This distillery offers tasting experiences and tours beyond the area's many wineries.

This forested preserve shared with Hunts Point offers old estate gardens, big trees, and a loop walk near the lake.
Road End Beach
This public access point provides a small spot to reach the Lake Washington shoreline.

This off street trail and sidewalk system links Yarrow Point with Hunts Point, Medina, and Clyde Hill.

Evergreen Rotary Park sits just north of downtown and offers beach access, a boat launch, and walking paths.

Brier City Hall
Brier City Hall sits along Brier Road, the city's main north-south route.
Brier Library

Locust Creek Park is a natural area in Brier popular for walking and hiking.

Ed Munro Seahurst Park

Tolt-MacDonald Park

Nick Loutsis Park
Nick Loutsis Park is a Carnation city park that includes a casual disc golf course.
Valley Memorial Park
Valley Memorial Park features a popular pump track for bikes, scooters, and skateboards.
River's Edge Park
River's Edge Park is one of the city's parks offering open space along the river valley.

Seminary Hill Natural Area
Seminary Hill Natural Area offers hiking trails and scenic views above the city.

Muromoto Memorial Park
Muromoto Memorial Park is a small pocket park offering a viewpoint and pedestrian access.

The Covington Historical Museum features exhibits on the city's early settlers and logging industry.

A marine science and technology center on the waterfront operated by Highline College.
Des Moines City Hall
The civic building that houses the city government offices.

An early twentieth century company town neighborhood listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
DuPont Historical Museum
A local history museum on Barksdale Avenue in a building that once served as a butcher shop and the first city hall.
Sellers Park

DuPont City Hall
The civic building on Civic Drive that houses city offices.
Snoqualmie Valley Trail

McCormick Park
A riverfront park along the Snoqualmie River with open space and river access.
Historic Dougherty Farmstead
A preserved pioneer era farmhouse maintained by the city as a heritage site.
Duvall City Hall
The civic building serving the city government.
Edgewood Community Park
A city park near 36th Street East and Meridian Avenue East that opened in 2022.
Edgemont Park
A wooded five acre park with a playground, ball diamond, basketball court, and picnic shelter.
Nelson Nature Park
A passive park set in a serene wetland area with native plants and wildlife.
Nyholm Windmill
A local landmark that is incorporated into the city's official logo.
Edgewood City Hall
The civic building on Dom Calata Way East that houses city offices.

A Washington State Ferries terminal with service across Puget Sound to Kingston.
Brackett's Landing
A waterfront park with a beach and the Edmonds Underwater Park marine sanctuary.
Edmonds City Park
A downtown park with a large playground and a seasonal spray park.

A public fishing pier on the waterfront at the end of Dayton Street.
Edmonds City Hall
The civic building that houses the city government offices.

Mud Mountain Dam Park

Enumclaw City Hall
The civic building on Griffin Avenue that houses city offices.

A bluff-top park with sweeping views of Port Gardner Bay and the Olympic Mountains.
Langus Riverfront Park
A park on the Snohomish River with a boat launch, fishing pier, and a paved trail.

A beach park on Puget Sound with an off-leash dog area and a playground.
Evergreen Arboretum and Gardens
A public garden with themed plantings, sculptures, and reflecting pools.
Everett City Hall
The civic building that serves as the seat of the city government.
Dash Point State Park
A 461 acre Washington state park on Puget Sound with sandy shoreline and forested hiking and biking trails.
Steel Lake Park
A popular city park with a lake, a swimming beach, picnic areas, and trails.
Town Square Park
A downtown park near the Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center.

Federal Way City Hall
The civic building that houses the city government offices.

Brookville Gardens Community Park
Brookville Gardens Community Park offers a pond, walking paths, and picnic areas.
Levee Pond Park
Levee Pond Park provides a pond and a walking trail for local residents.
Fife History Museum
The Fife History Museum shares the history of Fife and the surrounding area through exhibits and displays.

Prospector Park offers open space for leisurely strolls near town.

accesso ShoWare Center

Burke-Gilman Trail

Cavalero Community Park
